candidates.exact_span:
The facility is a POTW treating sanitary wastewater. POTW’s have technology based ELG’s
established at 40 CFR Part 133, Secondary Treatment Regulation. Pollutants with ELG’s
established in this Chapter are BOD5, TSS and pH.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the facility is classified as a POTW subject to Part 133 ELGs determines which parameters (BOD5, TSS, pH) have technology-based enforceable limits and associated monitoring expectations for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span:
BOD5 limits of 30 mg/L for the 30-day
average and 45 mg/L for the 7-day average and 85% percent (minimum) removal are found at 40
CFR §133.102(a).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes concentration-based 30-day and 7-day BOD5 limits plus a minimum percent-removal requirement; different readings of averaging period or removal applicability change which limit applies to a reported measurement and what monitoring is required to evaluate removal.

candidates.exact_span:
TSS limits, 30 mg/L for the 30-day average and 45 mg/L for the 7-day
average, and 85% percent (minimum) removal, are, also, found at 40 CFR §133.102(b).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Same as BOD5: concentration limits by averaging period and a percent-removal obligation whose interpretation affects applicable TSS limits and the monitoring needed to assess them.

candidates.exact_span:
ELG’s
for pH are between 6-9 s.u. and are found at 40 CFR §133.102(c).
candidates.computation_change_reason: States a technology-based pH range of 6–9 s.u.; if taken as the operative limit rather than the more restrictive WQS cited in footnote (2) and the table value 6.6–9.0, the applicable pH discharge limit for compliance comparison changes.

candidates.exact_span:
Regulations at 40 CFR
§122.45(f)(1) require all pollutants limited in permits to have limits expressed in terms of mass
such as pounds per day. When determining mass limits for POTW’s, the plant’s design flow is
used to establish the mass load.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Determines whether enforceable limits are mass-based (lbs/day) versus concentration-based (mg/L) and ties mass limits to design flow; a different reading changes which numeric column in the limit table governs compliance.

candidates.exact_span: Loading in lbs/day = pollutant concentration in mg/L * 8.345 lbs/gal * design flow in MGD
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the conversion from concentration limits to mass limits; alternative interpretation of constants, units, or inputs would change the derived enforceable mass limits used for comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Final Effluent Limits 6.67 MGD design flow
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the design flow used to derive mass limits; a different design-flow value or interpretation (design vs actual) would change applicable lbs/day limits.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section: fact_sheet, table: Final Effluent Limits
candidates.exact_span: Flow                       N/A                N/A               Measure MGD         Measure MGD
candidates.computation_change_reason: Indicates flow must be measured in MGD for both 30-day and 7-day averaging contexts; interpretation of this monitoring obligation affects whether flow reporting was required during FY2025.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section: fact_sheet, table: Final Effluent Limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: Presents parallel mass and concentration limits for 30-day and 7-day periods; which column is enforceable (and whether the 7-day mass value 2504 carries lbs/day units) changes the limit used to evaluate reported BOD5 results.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section: fact_sheet, table: Final Effluent Limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: A 30-day-only percent-removal floor with no 7-day counterpart; interpretation affects whether removal is an enforceable limit, what averaging applies, and how missing influent/effluent data for removal calculation should be classified.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section: fact_sheet, table: Final Effluent Limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: Same dual mass/concentration structure as BOD5; interpretation of which limit form and averaging period applies changes TSS compliance evaluation.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section: fact_sheet, table: Final Effluent Limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: Same removal-limit and monitoring-period ambiguity as BOD5 percent removal, affecting applicable TSS limits and semantics when removal-related data are absent.

candidates.locator: Page 7, Section: fact_sheet, table: Final Effluent Limits
candidates.computation_change_reason: States a single pH range of 6.6–9.0 standard units without 7-day/30-day distinction; interpretation of this as the operative limit (vs technology-based 6–9 or WQS cited in footnote 2) changes pH compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span:
(1) % removal is calculated using the following equation: [(average monthly influent concentration – average
    monthly effluent concentration) ÷ average monthly influent concentration] * 100.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the removal calculation method and implicitly requires monthly influent and effluent concentration data; different interpretation of averaging or required inputs changes compliance assessment, monitoring obligations, and classification of missing removal evidence.

candidates.exact_span:
(2) Stream segment specific (20.6.4.401 NMAC) WQS, which are more restrictive than pH technology-based
    limits, 6-9 s.u.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies a WQS pH range of 6–9 s.u. as more restrictive than technology-based limits; reconciling this with the table value 6.6–9.0 changes which pH limit is applied for exceedance determination.
